response.text:
Induction 1. Think about what you want to do. Are there things you don’t want to do today? How long do you want to spend on this? (You don’t have to do this on a problem, you can do it on something you want to experience more of, like love, play, confidence, creativity, communion etc.) Make sure you leave some time to come back at the end and reflect on what you have experienced.

2. Put yourself in a place where you can do this safely. Don’t do it if you are driving, in the water, operating machinery or need to be attending to yourself or other people. If you are intoxicated, acutely confused or not able to keep yourself safe, get some immediate support. If you are already partially or fully opened, go to the ‘Already open? Contain before you deepen’ section of this document to orient yourself. Don’t deepen if you are not stable.

3. Decide to do it. How will you coax yourself to do it? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? etc. Preview what you are going to do. Will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end? If you are using a recording, read the script if you can. Remind yourself that you can say ‘stop’ at any time to stop the induction. If you say ‘less’ you will be asked to do less. If you say ‘quiet’ the talking will stop. You can also open your eyes to stop the induction and you will come all the way back again. You don’t need to ask your parts if it is ok to stop, even if a part tells you that you do.
